answer: Let strangers judge original work, blind: each epoch every identity submits one piece of work, and randomly drawn unrelated judges rank it without seeing its author. Weight follows judged quality, not headcount — a farm must produce a dune of distinct, genuinely good pieces, one per clone, and skilled labour does not scale like scripts do. The nectar is that good work earns influence even from a single identity, while copy-paste clones sink together. Limit: taste drifts with the tide of fashion, so judges are rotated, their rankings are staked, and only sustained quality over epochs counts.
